content:
Nathan Jeffrey Cuffee (October 23, 1851–February 5, 1912) was a Montaukett author, folk historian, and tribal-rights advocate associated with Eastville in Sag Harbor. He co-authored the 1905 historical novel Lords of the Soil with Lydia Jocelyn and helped carry Montaukett memory and land-rights advocacy into public record.

Historical context

In the 1890s, Cuffee helped lead Montaukett advocacy for tribal rights and legal action connected with Indian Fields, Hither Woods, and North Neck. His work shows how Native public memory, literature, and land-rights activism continued into the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

References

  1. John A. Strong, The Montaukett Indians of Eastern Long Island, 2001.
  2. Gaynell Stone, The History and Archaeology of the Montauk.
  3. Nathan Cuffee and Lydia Jocelyn, Lords of the Soil, Boston: C. M. Clark Publishing Co., 1905.
why_this_matters: Nathan Jeffrey Cuffee connects Montaukett literary history with land-rights activism. His work as an author, folk historian, and advocate shows that Montaukett people continued to organize, write, and assert community rights in public long after colonial dispossession.
